BiblicalUsage: Hazar-addar, the enclosure of glory, is named once as a point on the southern border of Canaan, where the boundary turns from Akrabbim toward Kadesh-barnea and on to Azmon. It marks the edge of the land God was giving Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even the border towns matter to God, because the promise was drawn on a real map with real names. Hazar-addar sits on the line He set.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
